Then it’s a drive to Indiana to meet American goats cheese pioneer Judy Schad of Capriole dairy where he is encouraged to find a new way to enjoy Bourbon. After a brief stop at Saxelby Cheesemongers, a stall at New York City’s public market on the Lower East Side, Will travels to Oregon to discover the fascinating story behind Rogue River Blue, one of the oldest raw milk blue cheeses in the US.

After picking up a few of the region’s famous Moreton Bay bugs, Adam hops back in his 4WD and catches the ferry over to Moreton Island for some coastline cruising and cooking.

programme.sub-title: Australia - New South Wales North Coast
programme.desc: The north coast of New South Wales is a magnet for tree- and sea-change families escaping from city life. Adam starts his tour off at Stuarts Point, where he sees the first commercial lemon myrtle farm in Australia. Dropping by Yamba at the mouth of the Clarence River, Adam sources the famous Yamba prawns straight from the trawler. Heading further north to Byron Bay, Adam visits a must-see produce attraction, the Mullumbimby farmers’ market. Finally he cooks up his inspiration from this culinary road trip, a Pacific paella at the spectacular Byron Bay lighthouse, situated on Australia’s most easterly point.

programme.desc: If the name ‘Brie’ conjures up images of a mild creamy flat cheese covered with a pure white mould, chances are you have never experienced authentic Brie from Brie. Will visits the Ile de France region to learn more about the benchmarks of the style, Brie de Meaux and Brie de Melun, before visiting Brie’s close cousin, Chaource, in the Champagne region. programme.desc: Will’s cheese tour takes him across the United States to look at artisanal cheese in regions not normally associated with specialist cheese. Will learns first hand about the challenges of making farmstead washed-rind cheese in Virginia before meeting up with his old friend Ari at Zingerman’s Creamery in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Then it’s a drive to Indiana to meet American goats cheese pioneer Judy Schad of Capriole dairy where he is encouraged to find a new way to enjoy Bourbon. After a brief stop at Saxelby Cheesemongers, a stall at New York City’s public market on the Lower East Side, Will travels to Oregon to discover the fascinating story behind Rogue River Blue, one of the oldest raw milk blue cheeses in the US.

programme.title: Flat Out Food
programme.desc: Jenn discovers how lentils are a popular Saskatchewan crop that's often just shipped overseas. A farmer, a brewer and a chef are changing that for the better.

programme.title: Destination Flavour Down Under
programme.desc: It is one tropical surprise after another when Adam takes to the road around Rockhampton, beginning his trip at a petrol station that’s known for making the best crab sandwiches in the state. He meets a fourth-generation farmer producing ginger and watermelon, visits a couple who farm the macadamias they use in their ice-cream, and stops in at the famous Eumundi Markets, where he picks up ingredients for a magnificent golden pavlova. After picking up a few of the region’s famous Moreton Bay bugs, Adam hops back in his 4WD and catches the ferry over to Moreton Island for some coastline cruising and cooking.

programme.title: Great Chocolate Showdown
programme.desc: The remaining five bakers must rise to the occasion as they bake chocolate bread and use it to make a dessert deli sandwich. In the Elimination Challenge, the bakers look to the silver screen.

programme.title: Please Eat Slowly Bitesize
programme.desc: Victor shows how easy it is to make fresh noodles at home: all you need is flour, water and a little bit of time!

programme.title: On Country Kitchen
programme.desc: Mark and Derek visit a chicken farm with a view, take in an afternoon of fishing together and learn about the methode traditionelle of sparkling winemaking. Mark takes Derek sightseeing.

programme.title: Rachael Ray's Meals In Minutes
programme.sub-title: Spaghetti With Semi-dried Tomato Pesto & Broccolini
programme.desc: Semi-dried tomatoes, a fairly new staple in American grocery stores, are both bitter and sweet at the same time; they have big flavor, an easy chew and Rachael demonstrates how to use them as the star in her recipe for a pesto that's paired with broccolini and served with sausage.

programme.title: My Market Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt serves up a dish steeped in Polish and Croatian heritage, Sarma-Style Soup. Mike teams up with Farmer Catherine Velisha for more green greatness with fillet steak and Iceberg salad. Matt heads to the iconic Noosa Lifesavers Club for BBQ snapper with almond cream.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: Chicken is always a crowd-pleaser, so Lidia shares two easy stovetop recipes with two very different flavor profiles.

programme.title: Pati's Mexican Table
programme.desc: In Tekit, or The Capital of the Guayabera, Pati encounters a tale of sons going against their father's wishes to follow their own path. Pati meets Eliodoro Xicum, a farmer's son who went against his father to build a family business making the iconic Guayabera shirts. Then she meets his son, Elio, who chose to become a chef and created a dish that resembles a Guayabera in honor of his father.

programme.title: Silvia's Italian Masterclass
programme.desc: Easy, clever, and full of flavour- these quick Italian dishes are designed to beat the midweek slump and bring joy back to the dinner table.

programme.title: Italian Food Safari
programme.desc: Tonight, we join professional rock fisherman at dawn to learn why so many Italians are drawn to the sea to fish for dinner. Chef Robert Castellani shows Guy an ingenious way of baking snapper and explains why Sicilians put a coin in the mouth of the fish. Luciana Sampogna demonstrates taralli, while Fred Pizzini shares his recipe for duck ragu, which the whole family enjoys alfresco with some of the family's wines.

programme.title: America The Bountiful
programme.desc: No fruit helped build America more than the apple, often referred to as 'our democratic fruit'.

programme.title: Everyday Gourmet With Justine Schofield
programme.desc: Justine makes her steamed whole artichokes, Adam Swanson whips up some spiced lamb ribs and Massimo Mele cooks his Mamma Maria's pickled carrots.

programme.title: Great Chocolate Showdown

programme.title: Please Eat Slowly Bitesize
programme.desc: Victor shares how to prepare a whole fish, as well as some tips on how to steam a whole fish when you don't have a large enough steaming basket.

programme.title: Destination Flavour Down Under
programme.sub-title: Australia - New South Wales North Coast
programme.desc: The north coast of New South Wales is a magnet for tree- and sea-change families escaping from city life. Adam starts his tour off at Stuarts Point, where he sees the first commercial lemon myrtle farm in Australia. Dropping by Yamba at the mouth of the Clarence River, Adam sources the famous Yamba prawns straight from the trawler. Heading further north to Byron Bay, Adam visits a must-see produce attraction, the Mullumbimby farmers’ market. Finally he cooks up his inspiration from this culinary road trip, a Pacific paella at the spectacular Byron Bay lighthouse, situated on Australia’s most easterly point.

programme.title: Flat Out Food
programme.desc: Traditional foods that can be foraged or hunted have provided nourishment for the people of Ohtapamihowin for thousands of years. Jenn learns about some of these ingredients and their uses.

programme.title: On Country Kitchen
programme.desc: Mark and Derek visit a mushroom farm, help out at a community garden, and get their hands sticky in confectionary making. At Mount Keira lookout, Mark tells Derek the story of the mountain.

programme.title: Rachael Ray's Meals In Minutes
programme.sub-title: Spicy Charred Tomato Pasta With Hot Sausage Or Chickpeas
programme.desc: Rachael shows us how to spice up a charred tomato sauce and pasta dinner in two ways, in minutes. In one dish she's serving the pasta over sausage and in the other dish she pairs the pasta with chickpeas that are seasoned for heat.

programme.title: My Market Kitchen
programme.desc: Mike learns creamy tarragon chicken from author and food stylist Jacob Leung. Chef Tobie cooks BBQ quail with pancetta while Adam Walls pairs it with amazing Aussie wines. Matt serves up lemongrass beef in betel leaves with Southeast Asian flavours. Mike and David Mann camp and cook barramundi tail with chicken sauce.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: Lidia reminds us that the simple kind gesture of cooking for others can make a big impact.

programme.title: Pati's Mexican Table
programme.desc: Pati explores the vibrant streets of Yucatan's capital, Merida, in search of its flavours. She tries the best tacos in Merida at Wayane. The aroma of freshly made cookies lures her to Donde Fabric, where their globitos and bizcochitos are an important part of Mérida's mornings.

programme.title: Silvia's Italian Masterclass

And pastry chef Alexandra Rispoli shows how to mix and cook fragrant pistachio biscotti.

programme.title: Cheese Slices
programme.sub-title: Brie From Brie And The French Affineur
programme.desc: If the name ‘Brie’ conjures up images of a mild creamy flat cheese covered with a pure white mould, chances are you have never experienced authentic Brie from Brie. Will visits the Ile de France region to learn more about the benchmarks of the style, Brie de Meaux and Brie de Melun, before visiting Brie’s close cousin, Chaource, in the Champagne region. He then travels to the underground caves of Herves Mons to find out how this respected Affineur selects and matures cheeses to its optimum before calling in to see Pascal Beillevaire to get a few tips from the largest specialist cheese retailer in France.

Then she meets his son, Elio, who chose to become a chef and created a dish that resembles a Guayabera in honor of his father.

Luciana Sampogna demonstrates taralli, while Fred Pizzini shares his recipe for duck ragu, which the whole family enjoys alfresco with some of the family's wines.

programme.sub-title: Australia - New South Wales North Coast
programme.desc: The north coast of New South Wales is a magnet for tree- and sea-change families escaping from city life. Adam starts his tour off at Stuarts Point, where he sees the first commercial lemon myrtle farm in Australia. Dropping by Yamba at the mouth of the Clarence River, Adam sources the famous Yamba prawns straight from the trawler. Heading further north to Byron Bay, Adam visits a must-see produce attraction, the Mullumbimby farmers’ market. Finally he cooks up his inspiration from this culinary road trip, a Pacific paella at the spectacular Byron Bay lighthouse, situated on Australia’s most easterly point.

programme.desc: If the name ‘Brie’ conjures up images of a mild creamy flat cheese covered with a pure white mould, chances are you have never experienced authentic Brie from Brie. Will visits the Ile de France region to learn more about the benchmarks of the style, Brie de Meaux and Brie de Melun, before visiting Brie’s close cousin, Chaource, in the Champagne region. Then it’s a drive to Indiana to meet American goats cheese pioneer Judy Schad of Capriole dairy where he is encouraged to find a new way to enjoy Bourbon. After a brief stop at Saxelby Cheesemongers, a stall at New York City’s public market on the Lower East Side, Will travels to Oregon to discover the fascinating story behind Rogue River Blue, one of the oldest raw milk blue cheeses in the US.

After picking up a few of the region’s famous Moreton Bay bugs, Adam hops back in his 4WD and catches the ferry over to Moreton Island for some coastline cruising and cooking.

Adam starts his tour off at Stuarts Point, where he sees the first commercial lemon myrtle farm in Australia. Dropping by Yamba at the mouth of the Clarence River, Adam sources the famous Yamba prawns straight from the trawler. Heading further north to Byron Bay, Adam visits a must-see produce attraction, the Mullumbimby farmers’ market. Finally he cooks up his inspiration from this culinary road trip, a Pacific paella at the spectacular Byron Bay lighthouse, situated on Australia’s most easterly point.

programme.desc: If the name ‘Brie’ conjures up images of a mild creamy flat cheese covered with a pure white mould, chances are you have never experienced authentic Brie from Brie. programme.desc: Torres Strait Islander chef and owner of Mabu Mabu, Nornie Bero, cooks and talks through some of her favourite easy recipes, from quick picked octopus to fresh baked damper.

programme.desc: It's all about superb herbs as Refugee Ambassador Yaser Naseri and Special Representative to Australia for UNHCR, Dr. Carina Hoang, join Adam to celebrate Refugee Week.

programme.title: Cheese Slices
programme.desc: Will’s cheese tour takes him across the United States to look at artisanal cheese in regions not normally associated with specialist cheese. Will learns first hand about the challenges of making farmstead washed-rind cheese in Virginia before meeting up with his old friend Ari at Zingerman’s Creamery in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Then it’s a drive to Indiana to meet American goats cheese pioneer Judy Schad of Capriole dairy where he is encouraged to find a new way to enjoy Bourbon. After a brief stop at Saxelby Cheesemongers, a stall at New York City’s public market on the Lower East Side, Will travels to Oregon to discover the fascinating story behind Rogue River Blue, one of the oldest raw milk blue cheeses in the US.

programme.title: Flat Out Food
programme.desc: Jenn discovers how lentils are a popular Saskatchewan crop that's often just shipped overseas. A farmer, a brewer and a chef are changing that for the better.

programme.title: Destination Flavour Down Under
programme.desc: It is one tropical surprise after another when Adam takes to the road around Rockhampton, beginning his trip at a petrol station that’s known for making the best crab sandwiches in the state. He meets a fourth-generation farmer producing ginger and watermelon, visits a couple who farm the macadamias they use in their ice-cream, and stops in at the famous Eumundi Markets, where he picks up ingredients for a magnificent golden pavlova. After picking up a few of the region’s famous Moreton Bay bugs, Adam hops back in his 4WD and catches the ferry over to Moreton Island for some coastline cruising and cooking.

programme.title: Great Chocolate Showdown
programme.desc: The remaining five bakers must rise to the occasion as they bake chocolate bread and use it to make a dessert deli sandwich. In the Elimination Challenge, the bakers look to the silver screen.

programme.title: On Country Kitchen
programme.desc: Mark and Derek visit a chicken farm with a view, take in an afternoon of fishing together and learn about the methode traditionelle of sparkling winemaking. Mark takes Derek sightseeing.

programme.title: Rachael Ray's Meals In Minutes
programme.sub-title: Spaghetti With Semi-dried Tomato Pesto & Broccolini
programme.desc: Semi-dried tomatoes, a fairly new staple in American grocery stores, are both bitter and sweet at the same time; they have big flavor, an easy chew and Rachael demonstrates how to use them as the star in her recipe for a pesto that's paired with broccolini and served with sausage.

programme.title: My Market Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt serves up a dish steeped in Polish and Croatian heritage, Sarma-Style Soup. Mike teams up with Farmer Catherine Velisha for more green greatness with fillet steak and Iceberg salad. Matt heads to the iconic Noosa Lifesavers Club for BBQ snapper with almond cream.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: Chicken is always a crowd-pleaser, so Lidia shares two easy stovetop recipes with two very different flavor profiles.

programme.title: Pati's Mexican Table
programme.desc: In Tekit, or The Capital of the Guayabera, Pati encounters a tale of sons going against their father's wishes to follow their own path. Pati meets Eliodoro Xicum, a farmer's son who went against his father to build a family business making the iconic Guayabera shirts. Then she meets his son, Elio, who chose to become a chef and created a dish that resembles a Guayabera in honor of his father.

programme.title: Silvia's Italian Masterclass
programme.desc: Easy, clever, and full of flavour- these quick Italian dishes are designed to beat the midweek slump and bring joy back to the dinner table.

programme.title: Italian Food Safari
programme.desc: Tonight, we join professional rock fisherman at dawn to learn why so many Italians are drawn to the sea to fish for dinner. Chef Robert Castellani shows Guy an ingenious way of baking snapper and explains why Sicilians put a coin in the mouth of the fish. Luciana Sampogna demonstrates taralli, while Fred Pizzini shares his recipe for duck ragu, which the whole family enjoys alfresco with some of the family's wines.

programme.title: America The Bountiful
programme.desc: No fruit helped build America more than the apple, often referred to as 'our democratic fruit'.

programme.title: Please Eat Slowly Bitesize
programme.desc: Victor shares how to prepare a whole fish, as well as some tips on how to steam a whole fish when you don't have a large enough steaming basket.

programme.title: Destination Flavour Down Under
programme.sub-title: Australia - New South Wales North Coast
programme.desc: The north coast of New South Wales is a magnet for tree- and sea-change families escaping from city life. Adam starts his tour off at Stuarts Point, where he sees the first commercial lemon myrtle farm in Australia. Dropping by Yamba at the mouth of the Clarence River, Adam sources the famous Yamba prawns straight from the trawler. Heading further north to Byron Bay, Adam visits a must-see produce attraction, the Mullumbimby farmers’ market. Finally he cooks up his inspiration from this culinary road trip, a Pacific paella at the spectacular Byron Bay lighthouse, situated on Australia’s most easterly point.

programme.title: Flat Out Food
programme.desc: Traditional foods that can be foraged or hunted have provided nourishment for the people of Ohtapamihowin for thousands of years. Jenn learns about some of these ingredients and their uses.

programme.title: On Country Kitchen
programme.desc: Mark and Derek visit a mushroom farm, help out at a community garden, and get their hands sticky in confectionary making. At Mount Keira lookout, Mark tells Derek the story of the mountain.

programme.sub-title: Spicy Charred Tomato Pasta With Hot Sausage Or Chickpeas

Matt serves up lemongrass beef in betel leaves with Southeast Asian flavours. Mike and David Mann camp and cook barramundi tail with chicken sauce.

programme.title: Lidia's Kitchen
programme.desc: Lidia reminds us that the simple kind gesture of cooking for others can make a big impact.

programme.title: Silvia's Italian Masterclass
programme.desc: From golden street food to unforgettable pastas and classic sweets, this episode celebrates the soulful simplicity and bold flavours of southern Italy.

programme.title: Italian Food Safari

programme.title: America The Bountiful

programme.title: Ainsley's Taste Of The Bahamas
programme.desc: Ainsley explores the deep roots of Bahamian history. He rounds things off with a hearty island veggie stew pot and warm Johnny cake.

programme.title: Sergio Perera's Destination Noosa
programme.desc: Michelin-trained chef and world traveller, Sergio Perera, takes to Noosa on the Sunshine coast where he explores the plentiful food scene of the region. Cooking fresh and locally sourced dishes, and venturing along the coastline and surrounding hinterlands, Sergio will be joined by friends and the pioneers of the Noosa food scene.

programme.title: Come Dine With Me The Professionals
programme.desc: Today's brand new Come Dine With Me Professionals heads to Bristol where our first hosts are Mexican restaurant Dalia Cucina owner-chef Kirsty and front of house Tamsin.

programme.title: Torres Strait At Home
programme.desc: Torres Strait Islander chef and owner of Mabu Mabu, Nornie Bero, cooks and talks through some of her favourite easy recipes, from quick picked octopus to fresh baked damper.

programme.title: The Cook Up With Adam Liaw
programme.desc: To celebrate Refugee Week, Adam invites tennis legend Jelena Dokic and CommUnity Construction founder Hedayat Osyan to share their treasured tastes.

programme.title: Cheese Slices
programme.sub-title: Brie From Brie And The French Affineur
programme.desc: If the name ‘Brie’ conjures up images of a mild creamy flat cheese covered with a pure white mould, chances are you have never experienced authentic Brie from Brie. Will visits the Ile de France region to learn more about the benchmarks of the style, Brie de Meaux and Brie de Melun, before visiting Brie’s close cousin, Chaource, in the Champagne region. He then travels to the underground caves of Herves Mons to find out how this respected Affineur selects and matures cheeses to its optimum before calling in to see Pascal Beillevaire to get a few tips from the largest specialist cheese retailer in France.

programme.title: Great Chocolate Showdown
programme.desc: The final four home grow their chocolate and confectionary skills to create a delectable trifle terrarium. With one Elimination Challenge before the finale, the home bakers' nerves are hanging by a thread, as they create a 3-tiered suspended cake.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Former Strictly star and real-life Dragon, Sara Davies takes Robson Gorge walking in Teesdale to introduce him to her way of getting close to nature.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: Robson plays host to his Grantchester co-star Tom Brittney on a road trip around County Durham. Their mission to find peace and relaxation in the countryside finds the duo Dragon Boat racing on the river Wear before heading to a forest camp where they spend the night. In the hands of expert forager Andy, the actors find food for dinner in the wild plants of the woodland.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo strikes out to explore the Britain of his youth. He's a 'boomer', born in the decade after the end of the Second World War, and he recalls the optimism and excitement of rebuilding a nation exhausted by conflict. He'll relive the agony and the ecstasy of British Rail and marvel at the new society and culture emerging in post war Britain. He begins his journey at Preston's Fulwood Barracks in Lancashire.

programme.title: Ran
programme.desc: Recently arrived in Australia, Ran wants to get ahead but frustrated by a lack of opportunity, he finds himself drawn into a world of crime and violence. 'Ran' provides an insight into the issues facing many young people in the Australian African community.

programme.desc: Will’s cheese tour takes him across the United States to look at artisanal cheese in regions not normally associated with specialist cheese. Will learns first hand about the challenges of making farmstead washed-rind cheese in Virginia before meeting up with his old friend Ari at Zingerman’s Creamery in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Then it’s a drive to Indiana to meet American goats cheese pioneer Judy Schad of Capriole dairy where he is encouraged to find a new way to enjoy Bourbon. After a brief stop at Saxelby Cheesemongers, a stall at New York City’s public market on the Lower East Side, Will travels to Oregon to discover the fascinating story behind Rogue River Blue, one of the oldest raw milk blue cheeses in the US.

He meets a fourth-generation farmer producing ginger and watermelon, visits a couple who farm the macadamias they use in their ice-cream, and stops in at the famous Eumundi Markets, where he picks up ingredients for a magnificent golden pavlova. After picking up a few of the region’s famous Moreton Bay bugs, Adam hops back in his 4WD and catches the ferry over to Moreton Island for some coastline cruising and cooking.

Pati meets Eliodoro Xicum, a farmer's son who went against his father to build a family business making the iconic Guayabera shirts. Then she meets his son, Elio, who chose to become a chef and created a dish that resembles a Guayabera in honor of his father.

programme.desc: The north coast of New South Wales is a magnet for tree- and sea-change families escaping from city life. Adam starts his tour off at Stuarts Point, where he sees the first commercial lemon myrtle farm in Australia. Dropping by Yamba at the mouth of the Clarence River, Adam sources the famous Yamba prawns straight from the trawler. Heading further north to Byron Bay, Adam visits a must-see produce attraction, the Mullumbimby farmers’ market. Finally he cooks up his inspiration from this culinary road trip, a Pacific paella at the spectacular Byron Bay lighthouse, situated on Australia’s most easterly point.

programme.desc: If the name ‘Brie’ conjures up images of a mild creamy flat cheese covered with a pure white mould, chances are you have never experienced authentic Brie from Brie. programme.desc: The north coast of New South Wales is a magnet for tree- and sea-change families escaping from city life. Adam starts his tour off at Stuarts Point, where he sees the first commercial lemon myrtle farm in Australia. Dropping by Yamba at the mouth of the Clarence River, Adam sources the famous Yamba prawns straight from the trawler. Heading further north to Byron Bay, Adam visits a must-see produce attraction, the Mullumbimby farmers’ market. Finally he cooks up his inspiration from this culinary road trip, a Pacific paella at the spectacular Byron Bay lighthouse, situated on Australia’s most easterly point.
